_meta: A model turn with two parts -- a reasoning field (the model thinking out loud) and an action field (the tool call it actually committed to) -- used to show why the harness must execute only the calls in the action channel, never tool calls it finds by scanning the reasoning text. Modern models emit a chain-of-thought or scratchpad where they weigh options, and that text routinely names tools the model is considering but has not decided to run: 'I could call delete_account to reset it, but first let me check the status with get_status.' The reasoning is deliberation, not a decision. A harness that extracts tool calls by pattern-matching the model's whole output -- reasoning included -- will find and execute delete_account (merely contemplated) alongside get_status (actually chosen), running an action the model explicitly deferred, and if that action is destructive the harness has caused real harm from a thought. The action channel exists precisely to separate the two: the tool-calling API returns committed calls as structured data in a dedicated field, distinct from the free-text reasoning, and only that field is a decision. The fix is to dispatch strictly from the action channel and treat the reasoning as data to log, never as a source of executable calls. reasoning is the model's think-out-loud text; mentioned_tools are the tool names that appear in it; action is the structured tool call the model committed to; destructive_tools names the tools that cause irreversible harm. These are the fixture; what a text-scanning dispatcher would execute versus an action-channel dispatcher are computed.
reasoning: The account looks corrupted. I could call delete_account to reset it, but that is irreversible, so first let me check the status with get_status before deciding.
